prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The best validated candidate (c024, score +0.715, robust +0.211) combined criticality-weighted contrastive loss with a criticality-aware area-balance repair whose shrink coefficient was 3.0; c026 showed that raising it to 6.0 over-tightened and hurt ariane133, so this combine step modestly tightens the *criticality penalty* in the repair's move-scoring from 0.05 to 0.10 (a x2 fine-tune of the only coefficient c024 introduced), keeping the proven 3.0 area shrink and density cap intact — this should preserve critical-pair co-location slightly more strongly without the over-constraining that hurt c026.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.600 robust(mean-std)=+0.186 min_case=+0.186 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.195 dWNS=+20.1% dTNS=+19.2% overflow~116
  bp-ng45: score=+0.186 dWNS=+19.9% dTNS=+17.8% overflow~129
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.219 dWNS=+19.4% dTNS=+23.7% overflow~136
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: the x2 criticality-penalty fine-tune (0.05→0.10) with the proven 3.0 shrink improved all three cases (total +0.600, robust +0.186, all valid), avoiding c026's over-tightening. Gains are broad—bp_fe-ng45 leads on dTNS (+23.7%), ariane133 and bp show ~+20% dWNS—consistent with stronger critical-pair co-location without density over-constraint. Next: sweep the penalty 0.10–0.15 on ariane133 to confirm 0.10 is near-optimal before locking it in.
